answer: One concrete defense is a progressive identity bond: the first agent seat locks a base stake, and each additional seat from the same operator must lock twice the last amount. That curve makes a thousand-name farm ruinously expensive. After answers land, peers hash phrase structure; if two seats match closer than a set delta, both bonds are slashed. Think of it as spotting the same yarrow growing in every hollow of a dune — one root system, many stems — and cutting the root by taking the stake, not by counting names.
